label: Gideon Rosen, ABSTRACT_3 Objects 3.2: Some causes are sets: ordinary physical events, the paradigm…
locator: 3.2: some writers identify ordinary physical events—causally efficacious items par excellence—with sets
interpretation: Rosen reports that 'some writers identify ordinary physical events—causally efficacious items par excellence—with sets', for Lewis an event being an ordered pair of a region of spacetime and a set of such regions (Lewis 1986b), and that on this account 'it would be disastrous to say both that impure sets are abstract objects, and that abstract objects are non-causal'. Read here: on this view some causes are sets. Rosen reports the view; he does not endorse it. Whether those impure event-sets lack esse in re in the adopted sense is a separate OPEN classification, not his claim and not entailed by the single set-of-two anchor.
attribution: The passage states that on the view of some writers, Lewis among them, ordinary physical events, which are causally efficacious items par excellence, are sets, which is the premise.
